newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saint-Louis may take Ebro-Azucarera stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Saint-Louis may take Ebro-Azucarera stake - paper.

text.p: Saint-Louis may take a stake of around 24 percent in a new entity created by the future merger of Spain's largest sugar groups Ebro and Azucarera, Les Echos reported on Wednesday.
Saint Louis already owns, through its Generale Sucriere unit, a little over 20 percent of Azucarera, Spain's second-largest sugar group.
The new entity would process some 800,000 tonnes of sugar, representing 80 percent of Spain's quota in the European Union.
The transaction may be based on a price of 6,000 francs per tonne of quota sugar against 10,000 francs in France, Les Echos said
The Spanish government, long opposed to letting Saint-Louis play a significant part in the restructuring of the Spanish sugar industry, had now softened its position, it said.
"I have recently been told by the highest authorities that not only our unit Generale Sucriere was not undesirable but could be present in a substantial way," chairman Daniel Melin told Les Echos.
A company spokesman told Reuters that Saint-Louis had previously said that if there was a merger between Azucarera and Ebro, it wished to play a role as an industrial operator in that restructuring.
Since Saint-Louis already controlled over 20 percent of Azucarera, its likely stake in the future entity would be around that level, he said.
